messages.author: 4184023bb084c468
messages.subject: pandoc version 1.12.3 or higher is required and was not found
parts:
Hi,

I get this message when trying to build a package that has a knitr vignette:

pandoc version 1.12.3 or higher is required and was not found

This particular machine has pandoc version 1.9.1.1 installed.


apt-get install --only-upgrade  pandoc

says pandoc is already the newest version. I'm on ubuntu 12.04 and not yet ready to update to 14.04. I don't want to install pandoc from source because I always try to use package managers whenever possible.

Though I did try to install cabal as with 'apt-get install cabal' only to be told 'Unable to locate package cabal'.


Is there a way to add to my package repositories so I can get a newer version of pandoc? Or is there a way to work around the dependency on version 1.12.3?


Dan

messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] pandoc version 1.12.3 or higher is required and was not found
parts:
Hi Dan,

You can add Michael Rutter's PPA

sudo add-apt-repository -y ppa:marutter/c2d4u
sudo apt-get update

You should then be able to

sudo apt-get install pandoc pandoc-citeproc

Notes: This PPA also has ubuntu binaries for many recent CRAN
packages. If add-apt-repository isn't installed on your system, you
will need to run `sudo apt-get install python-software-properties`
first on ubuntu 12.04.

Cheers,

Carl

cabal update
cabal install pandoc

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] pandoc version 1.12.3 or higher is required and was not found
parts:
No, I do not think so. Its current version seems to be 1.12.3, which
is several versions behind the latest one. It might be very difficult
to make a standard Debian package for Pandoc, since I have tried
several times to find an up-to-date Pandoc package for Debian/Ubuntu
but failed. If someone knows such a PPA exists, please let me know.

Another way to get the Pandoc binary is through RStudio, which bundles
a version of Pandoc (1.12.4.2) with it. After you install RStudio, you
will get Pandoc under /usr/lib/rstudio/bin/pandoc/pandoc:
https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/master/PANDOC.md Of course,
this is not the latest version of Pandoc, either.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] pandoc version 1.12.3 or higher is required and was not found
parts:
The Rutter repository includes pandoc 1.12.3.3 and pandoc-citeproc
0.3.0.1 on the trusty mirror; I think more recent versions can be
built from source by cabal but don't know off the top of my head.
Michael seems to try and package Ubuntu binaries for many (but not
all) of the CRAN packages on that PPA, and thus usually has recent
binaries for the external dependencies such as pandoc that are used by
a variety of those packages. I don't know Michael personally and
can't vouch for how regularly that PPA is updated, or it's security
etc, but it certainly is handy for installing pre-built binaries for
pandoc and other CRAN packages; you'll see it in use on a lot of the
travis-CI setups for R packages for that reason (if you use that kind
of thing). Of course there's always a tradeoff between having a
binary and having the latest bleeding edge source build.

Digressing even further, I'll mention that I know use a containerized
environment for running all my R code by using Docker. This is
particularly easy / seamless if you're already running Linux, and it
makes it much easier to manage dependencies, port to other machines,
and avoid conflicts. For instance it makes it easy to launch a ubuntu
12.04 container and check what version is available in my previous
email, or have a container with all the necessary bits already
installed that you can move about to different machines, but that is a
discussion for a different list ;-)
